sense: of a person: free, not busy

terms.gloss: be free, have time, be at leisure
terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; with a dative, “have time for”
evidence: Cic. Att. 12.38.2: sīc scrībēs aliquid sī vacābis
Cic. Fam. 12.30.1: sī nē tū quidem vacās
Hor. Ep. 2.2.95: sī forte vacās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Philosophiae semper vacō, “I always have time for philosophy” (Cic. Div. 1.10, Lewis & Short). The impersonal vacat with an infinitive, “there is time to”, is poetic and post-Augustan. The opposite is occupātus, busy.

evidence: Cic. Off. 3.1: numquam sē minus ōtiōsum esse quam cum ōtiōsus

terms.gloss: be on hand, be at someone’s service
terms.grammar: with a dative of the person
evidence: Cic. Mur. 19: praestō multīs fuit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 4.1.4: ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō

phrases.latin: tū, quoniam necesse nihil est, sīc scrībēs aliquid sī vacābis
phrases.english: since there’s no need, just write a line if you have time

phrases.latin: aut, sī nē tū quidem vacās, nōlī impudēns esse
phrases.english: or, if you aren’t free either, don’t be shameless

phrases.latin: ibi mihi Tulliola mea fuit praestō nātālī suō ipsō diē
phrases.english: my little Tullia was there to meet me, on her very birthday

sources: Lewis & Short: vaco · Lewis & Short: otiosus · Lewis & Short: praesto
